summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on application integration details: SDK usage for tool+function calls, structured JSON output stability, and performance tradeoffs. Customer shared new payloads and raised concerns about strict schema validation, tokenization/stream truncation, and auditability (KMS + audit logs). Redwood team proposed benchmark plan and canary testing, and agreed to provide updated latency percentiles and pricing for a short Dedicated pilot.
topics: SDK snippets and recommended client-side retry/backoff
Function & tool calling patterns: webhooks vs sync RPC
Structured output JSON schema enforcement and validation failures
Performance: batching, streaming behavior, and KV-cache warmup
Security: VPC/private deployment vs hosted, SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call. lena from redwood and marcus is here.
[00:05] Marcus Chen: morning, thanks.
[00:07] Priya Das: hi, priya here. evan and sara also on.
[00:12] Evan Clarke: hey.
[00:13] Sara Molina: hi all.
[00:20] Lena Ortiz: high level agenda — 1) review results from last week's schema failure tests, 2) discuss SDK integration approach for function/tool-calls, 3) perf follow-ups and next steps.
[00:32] Priya Das: the big thing for us is deterministic structured output — we need the model to reliably emit the JSON we validated against our schema. last run we saw 7% parse failures because of missing fields and sometimes extra commas.
[00:44] Marcus Chen: yep, we looked into that — most of the failures were due to truncation at the end of stream and occasional hallucinated keys like "orderId" vs your field "order_id"; tokenization boundary issues. for truncation we recommend either longer response max-tokens with streaming or server-side post-repair heuristics.
[00:59] Evan Clarke: can you explain the repair heuristics? we prefer strict validation rejecting bad payloads, but we also don't want large partial failures.
[01:10] Marcus Chen: sure — two approaches: client-side strict validate and reject, or server-side repair which tries to re-run a small completion to close/open braces and fill missing keys with nulls. repair trades purity for success rate. we think schema-first prompts with function-calls helps. function-calls are ideal because the model returns structured args rather than free-text.
[01:30] Sara Molina: function-calls looked promising in the demo but we got occasional mismatched types — e.g., price returned as string. is that expected?
[01:38] Marcus Chen: sometimes yes — types can vary when model uses natural language. enforce types in the function schema and Redwood SDK will coerce/cast where safe or flag type errors. also recommend using explicit token-level instructions and partial validation.
[01:52] Priya Das: security question — for Dedicated pilot, do we get KMS integration and full audit logs? compliance needs SOC2+ and key separation.
[02:02] Lena Ortiz: yes — Dedicated includes KMS integration and audit logs. we can enable customer-managed keys (AWS KMS or HSM paths) and retention windows. i'll share the security pack after this call.
[02:15] Evan Clarke: what about VPC egress? our compliance team requires no internet egress for PII-containing payloads.
[02:23] Marcus Chen: for Aurora we recommend Private deployment in your VPC — that keeps inference in customer network. hosted API can be used for non-sensitive flows. note that on-prem or VPC deployment has a longer setup time.
[02:36] Priya Das: timeline wise, we need a pilot running in productionish by end of q3, ideally sept 15. is that feasible?
[02:44] Lena Ortiz: feasible if we lock scope this week. dedicate 3 weeks for infra setup + one week for canary testing. so starting in late august gets us to mid sept.
[02:54] Marcus Chen: on perf — we ran your batch of 500 sample requests through rwd-2-7b-q8 quantized on GP2 pools. numbers: p50 ~ 120ms per token, p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.2s for long sequences (2k). there's a warmup effect because of KV-cash load — i mean KV-cache.
[03:12] Evan Clarke: those p99s are a bit high for our latency SLO (under 700ms). can batching and streaming help lower observed tail?
[03:20] Marcus Chen: yes — reduce max-seq for interactive flows, leverage prefix caching for repeated context, and set autoscaling thresholds. also consider Dedicated capacity to reduce noisy neighbor effect; that shaves 10-30% off p95/p99 in our experience.
[03:36] Sara Molina: how does SDK handle function calls? we want simple webhook-style integration where model triggers an external tool (e.g., payment authorizer) and we need retry semantics.
[03:45] Marcus Chen: SDK supports two modes: synchronous function-calls where the model returns structured args to your app to call a tool, and asynchronous tool-calls where Redwood can proxy webhooks. for retries, SDK includes idempotency keys and exponential backoff helpers. we can share code snippets.
[04:00] Priya Das: we tried SDK v0.12 and saw occasional JSON parse errors in streaming mode — is that a known bug?
[04:07] Marcus Chen: there was a bug in early streaming buffer flush that could split JSON tokens across frames; fixed in v0.12.3. if you're on v0.12.1/2 upgrade to .3. i'll push a patch link.
[04:20] Evan Clarke: great. about structured output validation — will Redwood run schema checks before returning response to the app? or is that up to us?
[04:28] Marcus Chen: Redwood can optionally validate on the server edge and flag responses as validated, or return raw and let your app validate. server-side validation adds small overhead but decreases parse failures reaching your product. it's configurable per route.
[04:41] Lena Ortiz: quick demo note — marcus, can you summarize the demo we ran last thursday on the staging canary?
[04:46] Marcus Chen: sure — we ran function-calls for the refund flow. baseline: 200 requests with streaming, 98% succeeded with schema-validated outputs when using server-side validation + function schema. without server-side validation success fell to 89% due to truncation and type mismatches.
[05:02] Sara Molina: ok that matches what we saw. what's the minimal change to our prompt/template to improve reliability?
[05:08] Marcus Chen: two quick changes — 1) explicit function schema with types and required fields, 2) include an "output_format": "json" instruction and an end-marker token like "<END_JSON>" then truncate/repair on that marker. also set streaming chunk size to larger frames to avoid mid-token splits.
[05:25] Priya Das: can we get a sample SDK snippet for node/python that shows handling a function-call and then calling our internal tool?
[05:33] Marcus Chen: yes will share sample repo link. it's basically: call createCompletion with function schema, check response.type=="function_call", parse args, call your tool, then send tool result back via follow-up message. idempotency and verification on webhook return.
[05:48] Evan Clarke: about cost — do you have guidance on tradeoffs between hosted usage and Dedicated for this workload?
[05:55] Lena Ortiz: summary: hosted is simplest but noisy neighbor variance can impact tail latency. Dedicated has commit costs but predictable p95/p99 and supports private keying. we can run a short pricing scenario in the sheet.
[06:08] Marcus Chen: also quantization helps reduce cost; we used q8 on the rwd-2-7b which lowered token CPU and improved throughput. for higher accuracy flows consider rwd-3 variants which cost more.
[06:20] Priya Das: one of our legal asks is audit logs per token or per request with redaction. can Redwood provide that?
[06:27] Lena Ortiz: yes audit logs per request and per API key with token counts and timestamps; PII redaction is configurable. we'll include retention options in the security pack.
[06:38] Sara Molina: any blockers for next week?
[06:41] Marcus Chen: we need your sample payloads and schema v2 to run more targeted tests. also we'll run the 4k seq throughput test you requested.
[06:50] Evan Clarke: i'll get payloads by monday.
[06:52] Lena Ortiz: recap of next steps: lena sends security + pricing, marcus runs perf tests and shares sheet, evan pushes sample payloads and staging webhook.
[07:03] Priya Das: sounds good. thanks all.
[07:05] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links. bye.
[07:10] (call ends)

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings: "KV-cache" transcribed once as "K-V cash". references to docs: security pack link (internal): https://redwood.example.com/security/aurora-pack and benchmark sheet: https://sheets.example.com/aurora-poc-benchmarks. SDK snippet repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-samples/tree/aurora.
